name: Daikon radish (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Daikon radish (Raphanus sativus var. longipinnatus) [Vegetables] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 168451 (Radishes, oriental, raw; SR Legacy 11429) - full proximate, sugar total, vitamin, mineral, amino-acid and fatty-acid panel
Zaki et al., Front. Plant Sci. 2021, PMC8566945 - glucose:fructose:sucrose ratios in R. sativus roots (glucose > fructose >> sucrose)
Baenas et al., metabolic profiling of Raphanus sativus cultivars, PMC6273575 - TCA organic acids (malic, citric, succinic, fumaric) in root
Frontiers Nutrition 2022, fnut.2022.889407 - widely-targeted metabolomics of radish taproot organic acids (malonic, citric, oxalic dominant)
Gutierrez & Perez, Raphanus sativus chemistry review - oxalic, malic, malonic as principal root organic acids
provenance.curation_notes: Daikon root is a dilute (94.6% water), low-fat medium whose dominant carbon/energy source is free hexose sugars (glucose > fructose, total sugars 2.5 g/100g) plus organic acids (malic/malonic dominant, with oxalic low and citric/succinic/fumaric as TCA intermediates - all previously absent from the DB). The largest correction was the sugar profile: the current record listed only sucrose, which is actually the minor sugar. Amino-N is modest (0.6 g protein, glutamate-rich). Organic-acid fresh-weig
curation_added: D-glucose (dominant sugar, absent from current list)
D-fructose (second dominant sugar, absent from current list)
malic acid, malonic acid, oxalic acid, citric acid, succinic acid, fumaric acid (organic acids entirely missing)
quantified amounts for vitamin C, niacin, B-vitamins, minerals, amino acids, fatty acids
L-phenylalanine and L-valine (protein amino acids missing from current list)
corrected sugar picture: current DB listed sucrose as the ONLY sugar, but it is the least abundant

curation_removed.name: Retinol
curation_removed.reason: Preformed vitamin A (retinol) does not occur in plants; daikon root has only provitamin carotenoids (and those only in trace). FooDB/expansion artifact.

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Cobalt ion; ultra-trace, no measured value in daikon root and no plant requirement at nutritional level. FooDB predicted noise.

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Ultra-trace non-nutritive element, not measured in daikon root. FooDB predicted noise.

curation_removed.name: Chromium
curation_removed.reason: Ultra-trace element, not measured in daikon root. FooDB predicted noise.

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+)
curation_removed.reason: Redundant oxidation-state duplicate of iron; consolidated into single 'iron' entry.

curation_removed.name: Fe2+ mitochondria
curation_removed.reason: Compartment-tagged duplicate of iron (a modeling artifact, not a food nutrient); consolidated into 'iron'.

curation_removed.name: D-Serine
curation_removed.reason: D-enantiomer artifact; plant/protein serine is L-serine. Replaced by L-serine.

curation_removed.name: epsilon-Polylysine
curation_removed.reason: A microbial (Streptomyces albulus) food-preservative additive, not a native daikon metabolite. FooDB noise.

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: A furanocoumarin characteristic of Apiaceae/Rutaceae (celery, citrus), biologically implausible in Raphanus (Brassicaceae). FooDB predicted.

curation_removed.name: (±)-erythro-Isoleucine
curation_removed.reason: Stereochemical artifact of isoleucine; the real nutrient (L-isoleucine) is already listed.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
